'''''Trifolium angustifolium''''' is a species of [[clover]] known by the common names '''narrowleaf crimson clover''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TRAN6|taxon=Trifolium angustifolium|access-date=15 December 2015}}</ref> '''narrow clover'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''narrow-leaved clover'''.

==Description==
''Trifolium angustifolium'' is an annual herb growing erect in form. The leaves are divided into narrow leaflets which are linear to lance-shaped and measure up to {{Convert|4.5|cm|frac=4|sp=us}} long. The leaves have [[stipule]]s tipped with bristles. The herbage is hairy in texture.

The [[inflorescence]] is a cylindrical spike of flowers measuring {{Convert|1 to 5|cm|abbr=on|frac=4|sp=us}} long. Each flower has a group of [[sepal]]s (a ''calyx'') with long, hairy, needle-like lobes that harden into bristles as the plant dries. Within each calyx is a pink [[Corolla (botany)|corolla]] about 1 cm long.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native to Europe, Asia, and North Africa. It occurs in many types of habitat, including disturbed areas.

It can be found elsewhere as an [[introduced species]], including an [[invasive species]] in parts of North America, such as [[California]].
